headline: Daily market snapshot 2026-10-23
summary: US equities fell sharply on Thursday Oct 22 led by the Nasdaq (-2.6%) on AI-spending fears from Meta/Tesla earnings. Friday Oct 23 futures pointed modestly lower again. Oil extended its rally to Brent $113–114 and WTI near $100 on Houthi-Hormuz tensions; gold slid to ~$4,021; BTC fell to ~$81,600.
key_facts: Nasdaq closed Oct 22 at 26,008.86 (-2.60%) — worst day since June

headline: S&P 500, Nasdaq end sharply lower as revived AI doubts ignite tech selloff
summary: US stocks fell sharply on Thursday as fresh concerns over AI capital spending — triggered by Meta and Tesla earnings — drove the Nasdaq down 2.6% to 26,008.86, its worst session since June, while the S&P 500 lost 1.21% to 7,663.43. The Dow managed a marginal +0.02% gain.
key_facts: AI spending doubts from Meta/Tesla earnings drove selloff
Rising oil prices added inflation uncertainty

headline: US stock futures fall Friday after Nasdaq worst day since June
summary: US equity index futures declined Friday morning, with S&P 500 futures down 0.28% and Dow futures down about 316 points (0.59%), extending Thursday's tech-led selloff. Oil near $111 per barrel added pressure through inflation concerns.

headline: Meta Q3 2026 revenue up 26% to $64.6B; announces 2-for-1 stock split
summary: Meta Platforms reported Q3 2026 revenue of $64.601 billion (+26% YoY), beating consensus by roughly $1.26 billion. The company announced a 2-for-1 stock split via issuance of non-voting Class C shares, expected to trade in late January 2027. A large legal charge compressed GAAP operating income to $12.988B (−37%), but non-GAAP EPS reached an estimated $7.40.
key_facts: GAAP operating margin 20% vs 40% prior year
2-for-1 stock split (Class C non-voting), trading late Jan 2027

headline: Meta Platforms Q3 2026 8-K: $64.6B revenue, $12.988B operating income, 2-for-1 Class C split
summary: Meta's SEC 8-K filing for Q3 2026 confirms $64.601B revenue, GAAP diluted EPS of $3.83, and operating income of $12.988B. The filing details the 2-for-1 stock split via Class C non-voting shares and Q4 revenue guidance of $73–76B.

headline: TSLA Q3 earnings beat on auto margin gains; 2026 capex view cut
summary: Tesla reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.48, beating the $0.45 consensus estimate, on improved auto margins. Revenue came in at $28.046 billion, slightly below the $28.341 billion consensus estimate, with energy generation and storage a notable soft spot. Management cut its 2026 capital expenditure outlook.
key_facts: Stock -14.5% for the week heading into earnings

headline: Musk Says SpaceX and Tesla Have Begun Exploring a Merger, Committees Formed
summary: Elon Musk confirmed on SpaceX's October 20 earnings call that both Tesla and SpaceX have formed special committees of independent directors to study a potential merger. Musk said he cannot participate in the discussions as a conflicted party and that no deal terms have been agreed, cautioning that a merger may never happen.
key_facts: SpaceX and Tesla each formed special independent committees
Musk confirmed committees at shareholders' request
No deal terms agreed; merger may never occur
SpaceX shares +8% AH; TSLA +1.8% after announcement

headline: Tesla-SpaceX Merger Could Be Announced Before December, Barclays Says
summary: Barclays analyst Dan Levy identified Tesla's annual general meeting (expected no later than December 6) as a potential deadline for announcing a Tesla-SpaceX merger. Barclays estimated Musk could retain approximately 37% economic ownership and 56% voting control of a combined entity, though both shareholder groups would need to approve any deal.
key_facts: Barclays: announcement possible before Tesla AGM, by Dec 6
Musk estimated 37% economic ownership of combined entity
Both TSLA and SPCX shareholders would need to approve

headline: IBM delivers strong Q3, sees 4% to 5% revenue growth in 2026
summary: IBM reported Q3 2026 revenue of $17.1 billion, up 5% (6% at constant currency), beating consensus of $16.85 billion. Non-GAAP EPS of $2.95 beat estimates by $0.08. Software revenue grew 8% and management maintained its full-year constant-currency revenue guidance of 4–5%.
key_facts: Q3 revenue $17.1B +5% YoY (+6% CC), beat $16.85B consensus
FY2026 CC revenue growth guidance maintained at 4-5%

headline: IBM Q3 2026 Form 8-K: Revenue $17.1B, non-GAAP EPS $2.95
summary: IBM's SEC 8-K for Q3 2026 confirms revenue of $17.1 billion (+5% YoY), non-GAAP EPS of $2.95, and GAAP net income of $2.19 billion. Software rose 8%; IBM Z fell 20%; consulting was flat.

headline: Western Digital Q1 FY2027: Revenue $4.38B +55% YoY; non-GAAP EPS $4.64; stock falls ~5% AH
summary: Western Digital reported first-quarter FY2027 revenue of $4.38 billion, up 55% year over year, well ahead of estimates, with non-GAAP diluted EPS of $4.64 (up 161% YoY) and a non-GAAP operating margin of 49.1%. Despite the beat, shares fell approximately 5% in after-hours trading amid broader AI-related selling. The company raised its quarterly dividend 17% to $0.175 per share.

headline: Spotify Q3 2026: Revenue €5.0B in-line; premium subs 306M beat 305M guide; gross margin 32.9%
summary: Spotify's Q3 2026 results showed revenue of €5.0 billion (in-line with guidance), operating income of €670 million (in-line), and 306 million premium subscribers, slightly above the 305 million guidance. Gross margin of 32.9% came in marginally below the 33.0% target. Monthly active users reached 788 million, on track with guidance.

headline: Netflix tops Q3 profit forecast but trims two full-year targets as Q4 guide disappoints
summary: Netflix reported Q3 2026 earnings of $0.87 per share, beating the $0.82 estimate, with operating income up 37% to $4.46 billion on a 34.6% operating margin. However, Q4 revenue guidance of $13.44 billion and EPS guidance of $0.67 both missed estimates, and the company cut its FY2026 advertising revenue outlook to ~$2.7 billion from ~$3.0 billion, sending shares down ~5.7% in after-hours trading.
key_facts: FY2026 ad revenue cut to ~$2.7B from ~$3.0B

headline: Netflix Q3 2026 8-K: EPS $0.87, revenue $12.87B, Q4 EPS guide $0.67
summary: Netflix SEC filing for Q3 2026 shows diluted EPS of $0.87, revenue of approximately $12.87 billion, and guidance for Q4 EPS of $0.67 and revenue of $13.44 billion. Full-year advertising revenue guidance was trimmed and FCF guidance reduced.

headline: SpaceX Q3 2026: Revenue $14.6B, first-ever quarterly profit reported
summary: SpaceX reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $14.6 billion and posted its first-ever quarterly profit, announced on the October 20 earnings call. The results provided a positive backdrop for Elon Musk's announcement on the same call that Tesla and SpaceX had formed merger-exploration committees.

headline: CSX Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Higher Volumes and Pricing
summary: CSX Corporation reported Q3 2026 earnings of $0.57 per share, surpassing the Zacks consensus estimate of $0.52 by 9.6%, with revenue also above forecasts. Higher volumes and pricing drove the beat.
key_facts: Higher volumes and pricing drove outperformance

headline: KMI Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Natural Gas Pipeline Strength
summary: Kinder Morgan reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.35, beating the $0.33 consensus estimate, with revenue of $4.53 billion topping the $4.38 billion forecast. Natural gas pipeline operations drove the outperformance.

headline: NDAQ Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Index and FinTech Growth
summary: Nasdaq Inc. reported Q3 2026 non-GAAP EPS of $1.04, beating the $1.02 consensus estimate, with net revenue of $1.48 billion topping the $1.46 billion forecast. Index and FinTech segment growth drove outperformance.

headline: Live Oak Bancshares Q3 2026 EPS misses, revenue beats
summary: Live Oak Bancshares reported Q3 2026 EPS of $0.52, below the $0.66 estimate, largely due to a one-time $17 million charge. Revenue of $175.64 million beat the $168.11 million forecast.

headline: Brent rises to $113.8, WTI crosses $100 as Hormuz supply risks persist
summary: Brent crude rose to $113.8 per barrel (+0.6%) on Friday as Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and Hormuz shipping tensions kept supply concerns elevated. WTI crossed $100 per barrel, with the Brent-WTI spread widening to approximately $13–14. Houthi rebels also claimed strikes on Saudi Aramco facilities.
key_facts: Houthi attacks on Saudi Aramco infrastructure

headline: Brent Crude Oil Futures Exceed $114 Per Barrel Amid Geopolitical Fears
summary: Brent crude oil futures exceeded $114 per barrel on October 23, reaching their highest level since April or May 2026, driven by intensified US-Iran hostilities, tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, and Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure.
key_facts: US-Iran hostilities and Hormuz attacks driving premium
Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure as additional factor

headline: Iran-backed Houthis struck Saudi Aramco executive offices in Dhahran
summary: Iran-backed Houthi rebels struck Saudi Aramco's executive headquarters in Dhahran in mid-October 2026, with Saudi officials describing a 'limited fire.' The attack, combined with ongoing Hormuz tanker strikes and a Houthi naval blockade threat, has contributed to Brent crude surging above $110.
key_facts: Houthis struck Aramco executive offices in Dhahran
Saudi officials: 'limited fire', no production disruption
Also hit fuel depots; threatened naval blockade of Saudi Arabia

headline: Bitcoin falls to $81,668 as $635M ETF outflows drag Ethereum and XRP
summary: Bitcoin fell to approximately $81,668 on October 23, down about 1.7–3.8% in 24 hours, as spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $635.6 million in outflows and the Nasdaq's 2.6% drop triggered $431 million in leveraged liquidations. The 24-hour range was $80,989–$84,306, with analysts citing support at $81,000 and then $80,000.

headline: Bitcoin price $81,568 after $431M liquidations on Nasdaq selloff
summary: Bitcoin traded around $81,568 on Friday after $431 million in leveraged long positions were forcibly liquidated, driven by the Nasdaq's 2.6% decline on Thursday. The correlation between tech equity selloffs and crypto market pressure remained elevated.

headline: Gold slides as safe-haven demand shifts to US Treasuries despite lower yields
summary: Gold fell below $4,050 on October 22 as safe-haven flows shifted to US Treasuries amid the equity selloff, despite yields declining. Kitco showed gold at $4,021.20 early Friday, near its lowest level since early August 2026. The DXY dollar index held around 101.62.
key_facts: Fell below $4,050 on Oct 22 — lowest since early August
Safe-haven flows moved to Treasuries instead

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield falls 15bps to 4.963% amid equity selloff safe-haven bid
summary: The US 10-year Treasury yield dropped 15 basis points to 4.963% on Thursday as safe-haven demand surged amid the equity selloff. The move lower in yields contrasted with gold's decline, suggesting Treasuries captured most of the flight-to-safety bid.
key_facts: Safe-haven bid drove Treasury demand despite gold decline

headline: Fed Oct 28 FOMC: Hold at 94% probability, rate hike odds fall to ~6%
summary: Markets have sharply repriced the Federal Reserve's October 28 decision toward a hold, with prediction markets (Kalshi, Polymarket) showing approximately 94% probability of no change and only 6% for a 25bp hike. The Fed's current target range is 3.75%–4.00%. December remains the more likely window for any further tightening.
key_facts: Rate markets repriced after bond traders backed off hike bets

headline: Reuters: Anthropic IPO investors push valuation down to $1.5T from $2T over Q3 growth slowdown
summary: Reuters reported that investors in Anthropic's upcoming IPO are pushing for a lower valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion, down from the $2 trillion previously targeted, citing slower Q3 revenue growth of 45% ($16.8B) compared to Q2's near-doubling. The IPO is now expected in November 2026; Anthropic's S-1 was filed June 1, 2026.
key_facts: Anthropic IPO valuation pushed to $1.5T from $2T
Q3 revenue $16.8B (+45% YoY vs Q2 near-doubling)

headline: SMCI Stock Gains Most In Nearly 2 Months On New Vera Rubin Racks, Analyst Upgrade
summary: Super Micro Computer (SMCI) rose 9.5% on October 22, its largest gain in nearly two months, after announcing it had begun shipping Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 racks (72 GPUs per rack, scalable to 1,152 GPUs in a 16-rack configuration with 331 TB of HBM4 memory) alongside an analyst upgrade.
key_facts: SMCI +9.5% — largest gain in nearly 2 months
Began shipping Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 racks
NVL72 rack: 72 Rubin GPUs, 36 Vera CPUs

headline: Nvidia falls 4.40% to $212.21 as AI spending fears drag chip stocks lower
summary: Nvidia closed October 22 at $212.21, down 4.40% on the day, as fresh doubts about the sustainability of AI capital spending — highlighted by Meta's $135–145B FY2026 capex guidance — weighed on semiconductor stocks broadly.
key_facts: AI spending concerns from Meta capex guidance dampened sentiment

headline: AI Chip Stocks Lose $2 Trillion in Eight Days Before Nvidia, AMD and Micron Stage Sharp Recovery
summary: After an 8-day rout that wiped approximately $2 trillion from AI chip stocks — triggered by CXMT's 4F² DRAM announcement — Nvidia, AMD, and Micron staged a sharp recovery starting October 19. Intel rose ~6%, AMD ~4%, and Nvidia ~2% in the initial rebound session, though gains were uneven as the overhang of AI spending concerns persisted into the following week.
key_facts: $2T wiped from AI chip sector over 8 days (Oct 8–16)
JPMorgan upgraded Intel on improved execution (Oct 19)
Gains uneven; NVDA retreated -4.4% by Oct 22

headline: Global markets retreat as tech mood sours, oil prices jump
summary: Asian equity markets retreated Friday, tracking the Nasdaq's 2.6% plunge, with the Nikkei 225 falling approximately 2.7% to 63,907. European markets also declined, with the DAX down around 1.1% to 25,372. Rising oil prices near $111–114 per barrel amplified the negative sentiment.

headline: Nikkei 225 drops as US tech selloff hits global sentiment; FTSE and DAX lower
summary: European indices fell Friday morning following Wall Street's tech-led selloff. The Frankfurt DAX was down roughly 1.1% and London's FTSE 100 was lower. On the prior session (Oct 21 close), the Nikkei had been at 64,621.24, DAX at 25,645.04, and FTSE 100 at 10,752.88 before the US selloff hit Thursday.
key_facts: Oct 21 prior session: Nikkei 64,621 +0.85%, DAX 25,645 +1.35%, FTSE 10,753 +0.19%

headline: Meta's $135–145B FY2026 capex guidance reignites AI spending sustainability debate
summary: Meta's announcement of $135–145 billion in FY2026 capital expenditures — following similarly elevated AI investment guidance from other Mag7 companies — reignited investor debate about the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending. The combination of Meta and Tesla earnings is seen as the primary trigger for the Nasdaq's 2.6% selloff on October 22.
key_facts: Reignited debate over AI spending returns
Nasdaq -2.6% on Oct 22 primarily attributed to Meta/Tesla earnings
Mag7 combined AI capex estimated in hundreds of billions

headline: Commerce Bancshares beats Q3 earnings, misses on revenue
summary: Commerce Bancshares reported Q3 2026 EPS of $1.08, beating the $1.07 consensus estimate, but revenue of $494.3 million fell short of the $498.4 million forecast.

headline: CME Group Q3 2026 beats on earnings and revenue
summary: CME Group reported Q3 2026 results that beat both earnings and revenue expectations, supported by elevated trading volumes amid market volatility driven by geopolitical tensions and interest rate uncertainty.
key_facts: CME Group Q3 beat on earnings and revenue
Elevated trading volumes amid market volatility

headline: AT&T Q3 beat with subscriber growth but stock falls ~4% on elevated AI infrastructure costs
summary: AT&T reported Q3 2026 results that beat on subscriber additions, yet the stock fell approximately 4% after the print, suggesting investors focused on capital spending pressures related to network AI infrastructure amid the broader market AI-spending debate.
key_facts: AI infrastructure cost concerns weighed on sentiment

headline: Western Digital falls ~5% after hours despite Q1 FY2027 earnings beat amid AI sector selloff
summary: Despite Western Digital's strong first-quarter FY2027 results — revenue up 55% and non-GAAP EPS up 161% — shares fell approximately 5% in after-hours trading on October 22, reflecting the broader AI-related selloff that also punished other semiconductor-adjacent stocks.
key_facts: WDC -5% AH despite strong earnings beat
Broader AI selloff overcame positive results

headline: Brent-WTI spread widens to $13–14 as seaborne oil premium surges on Hormuz tensions
summary: The Brent-WTI crude oil spread widened to approximately $13–14 per barrel as seaborne supply concerns from Hormuz tanker attacks pushed a premium onto internationally-delivered Brent grades. WTI, reflecting landlocked US production, traded near $100 while Brent exceeded $113.
key_facts: Seaborne premium from Hormuz tanker attack risk

headline: Sallie Mae Q3 2026 EPS loss of $0.19 on revenue of $616.5M, well below expectations
summary: Sallie Mae reported a Q3 2026 loss of $0.19 per share on revenue of $616.48 million, well below analyst expectations, alongside the wave of after-hours earnings reports on October 22.

headline: Alphabet (GOOGL) Q3 2026 earnings expected October 28; Amazon (AMZN) October 29
summary: The next major earnings catalysts are Alphabet (Q3 2026) expected October 28 and Amazon (Q3 2026) expected October 29, with both reports set to provide key data points on cloud and AI infrastructure spending trends that have driven this week's market volatility.
key_facts: Both reports key for AI capex narrative
July quarter: Alphabet +24% rev but -15% AH on capex; MSFT Azure +43% beat; AWS +37%

headline: Delta Air Lines Q3 2026 adjusted EPS $1.72 misses $1.80 estimate on fuel costs
summary: Delta Air Lines reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.72, missing the $1.80 consensus estimate. Adjusted revenues climbed 16% year over year to $17.59 billion but missed the $17.74 billion consensus by 0.9%, as elevated jet fuel costs from Hormuz-driven oil prices pressured margins.
key_facts: Fuel costs elevated by Hormuz oil premium

headline: Tesla Q3 earnings beat as margins and cash flow surprise, revenue narrowly misses
summary: Tesla's Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.48 beat the $0.45 estimate as auto margins and cash flow surprised to the upside, but revenue of $28.046 billion narrowly missed the $28.341 billion consensus. The energy generation and storage segment was the key soft spot, while management trimmed capital expenditure guidance.
key_facts: Adj EPS $0.48 beat $0.45; margins and cash flow surprised positively

headline: Intel, AMD and Nvidia Lead Chip Stocks Rebound After Brutal Selloff
summary: Chip stocks led by Intel (+6%), AMD (+4%), and Nvidia (+2%) staged a rebound on October 19 after an 8-session selloff that erased approximately $2 trillion in market value, triggered by CXMT's 4F² DRAM announcements. Analysts highlighted agentic AI and GPU supply shortages as potential positive catalysts despite lingering capex concerns.
key_facts: JPMorgan upgraded Intel on improved execution
Agentic AI and GPU shortages cited as upside catalysts

headline: Meta Announces Stock Split as Earnings Beat Drives Stock Back to $700 Level
summary: Meta announced a 2-for-1 stock split via issuance of non-voting Class C shares following its Q3 beat, with trading in the new shares expected to begin in late January 2027. The split is structured as a share issuance rather than a traditional split, with the non-voting shares intended to support capital raises, employee compensation, and acquisitions. Stock approached the $700 level post-announcement.
key_facts: 2-for-1 stock split via Class C non-voting shares
Non-voting shares support capital raises and employee comp

headline: Elon Musk says SpaceX-Tesla merger is 'a good idea' as companies form deal committees
summary: Elon Musk called a potential SpaceX-Tesla merger 'a good idea' on SpaceX's Q3 earnings call, while both companies simultaneously disclosed the formation of independent special committees to evaluate a combination. Musk emphasized he is a conflicted party and cannot negotiate terms himself.

headline: Crypto Prices Today: Bitcoin steady near $81,600 despite Iran tensions and AI selloff
summary: Bitcoin held relatively steady near $81,600 on Friday despite twin headwinds: Iran-related geopolitical tensions driving oil higher and a 2.6% Nasdaq selloff linked to AI spending concerns. Market cap was approximately $1.64 trillion.
key_facts: Holding despite Iran tensions and AI selloff

headline: Gold at $4,021.20 per ounce on October 23 — lowest since early August
summary: Gold traded at $4,021.20 per troy ounce early on October 23, near its lowest level since early August 2026, as safe-haven demand shifted toward US Treasuries and oil-driven inflation fears dampened traditional gold appeal.
key_facts: Safe-haven flows favored Treasuries over gold

headline: Fed October 2026 rate decision: Hold expected at 3.75-4.00%; December hike 94% odds
summary: Markets expect the Federal Reserve to hold rates at 3.75%–4.00% at the October 28 meeting, with CME FedWatch showing approximately 83% probability of no change and 17% probability of a hike. By year-end, a hike carries about 94% odds, suggesting December is the more likely timing for further tightening.

headline: UK CPI 3.5% October 2026; DXY edges lower as inflation surprise reduced BOE hike urgency
summary: UK CPI came in at 3.5% in October 2026, contributing to a slight dip in the US Dollar Index (DXY) toward 101.62 as markets reassessed global inflation and central bank rate paths. The data reinforced market expectations that the Bank of England may moderate its hiking pace.
